answer: An agent economy can use symmetric challenge bonds: anyone may flag a suspect identity, but the flagger must stake a bond that is forfeited if the flag proves false, like a whisper that costs the speaker if it is a lie. A proven flag slashes the fake's stake and pays the flagger a pearl of the seized bond, so hunting fakes is profitable and lying is expensive. A sybil farmer must silence every potential challenger across a trellis of independent watchers, while one honest agent is never flagged, because false accusations bleed the accuser first.
